html:
SMTO-DB-0014 — The database server address is missing or written wrongly

GUID: a4de553c-9eef-4afd-a56c-cd882fe34189
Slug: database-discovery-host-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server, but the server's address was empty or contained characters an address can't have. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Put just the server's name or IP address in the host field, for example db.example.internal or 10.0.0.5. SMTO only accepts letters, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores and colons in this field.
  2. Remove anything extra, such as "postgres://", a user name, a password, "@", slashes or spaces. A full connection link isn't a valid host, and passwords placed there could be exposed.
  3. Put the port, user and password in their own fields, then send the request again. Nothing was attempted the first time, so it's safe to send again once the address is right.

What success looks like

  • The search connects to the server and lists the databases it found as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages the database for its exact host name or IP address. If you share the request for help, leave out the password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request had an empty host (missing_host) or a host that fails the hostname/IP pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$ (invalid_host), so no connection was attempted.

What this means

  • The discovery host is empty or fails the bounded hostname/IP syntax check. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • The discovery host is empty or fails the bounded hostname/IP syntax check.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect only the host component and keep port, connection options and credentials in their own fields.

How to fix it

  • Set host to a bare hostname or IP address using only letters, digits, dots, hyphens, underscores and colons (for example db.example.internal or 10.0.0.5). Do not send a connection string or URL (postgres://...), a path, spaces, or user:password@ in host; send port, user and password in their own fields.
  • Supply the intended hostname or IP address, without connection-string syntax or credentials.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended hostname or IP passes request validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
